title: Polynomial deformation of an affine-space automorphism to its linear part
statement: Let k be a field, let d be a nonnegative integer, and put S=Spec(k). Use the concrete affine coordinate tower X_d(S), projection p_d(S), base-change maps X_d(f), and coordinate linear map a_g of [def-amb-affine-trace-tower] and [def-amb-affine-linear-trace-action]. For every automorphism e:X_d(S)≅X_d(S) with e.hom followed by p_d(S) equal to p_d(S), there are g in GL_d(Γ(S,O_S)) and an automorphism E of X_d(A¹_S) over A¹_S such that X_d(zeroSection) followed by E.hom equals a_g followed by X_d(zeroSection), and X_d(oneSection) followed by E.hom equals e.hom followed by X_d(oneSection). The sections are the actual coordinate-zero and coordinate-one sections of the parameter line. No cohomology or coefficient data occur.

source.place: Lemma 3.1, proof, pp. 5–6: translation and deformation to the linear part; characteristic-independent coordinate verification written by M2; compare Blanc, Conjugacy classes of special automorphisms of the affine spaces, introduction, pp. 939–940, https://msp.org/ant/2016/10-5/ant-v10-n5-p01-p.pdf

proof.text: Use the canonical affineTraceAffineSpaceIso and AffineSpace.SpecIso to write e in polynomial coordinates as F=(F_1,...,F_d), with inverse G. Set b=F(0). In k[t,x_1,...,x_d] define H_j=(F_j(tx)-b_j)/t+t b_j. This is a polynomial because each nonconstant monomial of F_j acquires a positive power of t and the constant term was subtracted.

Define J_j=G_j(t y+(1-t²)b)/t. The numerator at t=0 is G_j(b)=0, so polynomial division by t has zero remainder. Over k[t,t⁻¹,x] substitution gives t J(t,H(t,x))=G(F(tx))=tx and H(t,J(t,y))=(F(G(ty+(1-t²)b))-b)/t+t b=y. Since k[t,x] is a domain, the localization at t is injective, and both composition identities hold in the polynomial ring. Thus H and J define inverse k[t]-scheme morphisms.

At t=1, H is F. At t=0, H is the linear part of F-b, with matrix L. The specialization J(0,y) is also linear, since its numerator has first-order coefficient DG(b)y. Specializing both inverse identities makes these two matrices inverse. Regard L as a unit in the matrix ring over k, transfer its entries through Γ(Spec k,O)≅k, and call the resulting invertible matrix g. Transport H and J through the canonical affine-space/tower isomorphisms. The coefficients lie in k[t], so the resulting E lies over the parameter line. Equality on the projection and each coordinate proves both required endpoint equalities and identifies H(0,x) with the already defined affineTraceLinearMap. For d=0, use the identity family and the unique empty invertible matrix. Every computation uses only polynomial identities and works in positive characteristic.

theorem affineSpace_polynomial_deformation
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (d : ℕ)
    (e : affineTraceTower (Spec (.of k)) d ≅ affineTraceTower (Spec (.of k)) d)
    (he : e.hom ≫ affineTraceProjection (Spec (.of k)) d =
      affineTraceProjection (Spec (.of k)) d) :
    ∃ (g : Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin d) Γ(Spec (.of k), ⊤))
      (E : affineTraceTower (AffineSpace PUnit.{u + 1} (Spec (.of k))) d ≅
        affineTraceTower (AffineSpace PUnit.{u + 1} (Spec (.of k))) d),
      E.hom ≫ affineTraceProjection (AffineSpace PUnit.{u + 1} (Spec (.of k))) d =
        affineTraceProjection (AffineSpace PUnit.{u + 1} (Spec (.of k))) d ∧
      affineTraceMap (AffineSpace.zeroSection PUnit.{u + 1} (Spec (.of k))) d ≫ E.hom =
        affineTraceLinearMap (Spec (.of k)) d g ≫
          affineTraceMap (AffineSpace.zeroSection PUnit.{u + 1} (Spec (.of k))) d ∧
      affineTraceMap (AffineSpace.oneSection PUnit.{u + 1} (Spec (.of k))) d ≫ E.hom =
        e.hom ≫ affineTraceMap
          (AffineSpace.oneSection PUnit.{u + 1} (Spec (.of k))) d
